title: God's Smuggler
author: Brother Andrew with John and Elizabeth Sherrill
target_audience: Those interested in Cold War-era history
Teens and adults seeking stories of courage and faith
core_themes: Courage in the face of danger
primary_purpose: To recount the true story of Brother Andrew’s daring missions to smuggle Bibles and aid Christians behind the Iron Curtain, illustrating how faith, prayer, and courage can overcome great obstacles.

structure_format.organization: Chronological, interspersed with anecdotes and reflections; follows Brother Andrew’s early life, calling, and missions into communist Eastern Europe
features: Historical context of the Cold War
Accounts of miracles and narrow escapes

key_concepts_lessons: Ordinary individuals can make extraordinary impact through faith and conviction.
Faith in God can inspire incredible courage and resourcefulness.
Persecuted believers under oppressive regimes benefit tremendously from outside support—spiritual and material.
Prayer can produce tangible, even miraculous, results.
Taking risks for a higher purpose can change lives—both for those who risk and those they serve.
notable_features: Vivid first-hand accounts of smuggling Bibles across closed borders
Insight into the lives of Christians in the Soviet Bloc
Role of prayer and spirituality in high-risk situations
Catalyst for the global Open Doors ministry
cultural_historical_context: Written during the Cold War when religious persecution in communist countries was a pressing issue, the book inspired Western Christians to support the persecuted church worldwide. It highlighted the lack of religious freedom under communist regimes and the importance of underground missionary efforts.
reception_impact: International bestseller translated into over 30 languages
Raised widespread awareness and support for persecuted Christians
Helped launch Open Doors, a major missionary organization
Still cited as a foundational text in Christian missions literature
Critically acclaimed for its gripping narrative and authenticity
comparable_titles: The Hiding Place by Corrie ten Boom
Tortured for Christ by Richard Wurmbrand
Through Gates of Splendor by Elisabeth Elliot
